# Dotkernel | Headless Platform for modern web applications

> dotkernel.com is the technical blog for the Dotkernel headless PHP platform - a PSR-15 compliant application built on Mezzio and Laminas components. It publishes architecture write-ups, how-tos, and release notes for the platform applications - Dotkernel API, Admin and Queue - and for the standalone Dotkernel Light skeleton.

Content spans foundational PHP/middleware architecture (PSR-7, PSR-15, request lifecycle, dependency injection), practical how-tos (Doctrine migrations, CORS, authentication, caching), and the history/release notes of the Dotkernel ecosystem going back to 2008. Posts are organized by category and attributed to an author; URLs follow the pattern `/{category-slug}/{post-slug}/`. Each post also has a Markdown version at `/{category-slug}/{post-slug}.md`.

## Docs

- [OSS Package Lifecycle](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-packages-oss-lifecycle.md): support/maintenance status of Dotkernel's open-source packages
- [Architecture](http://localhost:8080/architecture.md): The PSR-15 middleware pipeline behind Dotkernel API, stage by stage: error boundary, routing, content negotiation, deprecation headers, OAuth 2.0, RBAC and dispatch - plus the library flow underneath it.
- [Development Environment](http://localhost:8080/wsl2.md): AlmaLinux 10 on WSL 2 for a RHEL-compatible local stack. One Ansible playbook installs PHP, Apache, MariaDB, Composer, Node.js and phpMyAdmin, and provisions a virtualhost for every project you add.
- [dotboost](http://localhost:8080/dotboost.md): dotboost is a drop-in .claude/ directory that teaches Claude Code the conventions of any Dotkernel application - ten commands, seventeen skills, six hooks, and permission guardrails that keep secrets out of the context.

## Pages

- [About us](http://localhost:8080/about.md): Dotkernel is built by the dev team at Apidemia - a team that reviews every change together, gives its work back to the PHP community under MIT, and puts guardrails around the tools it adopts.
- [Contact](http://localhost:8080/contact/): Get in touch, report a security issue, or find where to ask a question and contribute to the project.
- [Dotkernel - A Headless Platform for Modern Web Applications](http://localhost:8080/index.md): Dotkernel is a collection of open-source PHP application skeletons built on Mezzio and Laminas, ranging from a minimal presentation-site skeleton to a full headless platform (API, Admin, Queue) for enterprise-grade applications.
- [Dotkernel Admin](http://localhost:8080/admin.md): Dotkernel Admin is an open-source admin application (skeleton) built on Mezzio, Laminas and Doctrine. Table-based record management, RBAC guards, CSRF-protected forms and 2FA, over the same Core as Dotkernel API.
- [Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/api.md): Dotkernel API is an open-source REST API skeleton built on Mezzio, Laminas and Doctrine. OAuth2, RBAC, HAL, problem details and OpenAPI 3.0 come wired together on install. MIT licensed.
- [Dotkernel Frontend](http://localhost:8080/frontend.md): Dotkernel Frontend is a web starter skeleton on Mezzio and Laminas - user accounts, a contact form, RBAC guards, CSRF-protected forms, flash messages and GDPR account anonymization, server-rendered in Twig.
- [Dotkernel Light](http://localhost:8080/light.md): Dotkernel Light is a minimal PSR-15 application skeleton on Mezzio and Laminas, for presentation sites and small services. Six direct dependencies, Twig templating, Vite assets, no database layer.
- [Dotkernel Queue](http://localhost:8080/queue.md): Dotkernel Queue runs time-consuming work on background workers instead of inside the request cycle. A Swoole TCP daemon, Valkey streams and Symfony Messenger, with retries, a dead letter queue and reporting commands.

## Headless Platform

*the current Dotkernel headless architecture*

- [Complementary Admin in Dotkernel Headless Platform](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/complementary-admin-in-dotkernel-headless-platform.md): Overview of Dotkernel Admin, the independent, first-party admin application designed to pair seamlessly with Dotkernel API in the Dotkernel Headless Platform.
- [Dotkernel API v6: The root of Dotkernel Headless Platform](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/dotkernel-api-v6-the-root-of-dotkernel-headless-platform.md): Overview of what changed in Dotkernel API v6 since the original architecture and components article, covering new features, the Core module, composer updates, and testing/configuration changes.
- [Dotkernel Headless Platform - The Whats, Hows and Whys](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/dotkernel-headless-platform-the-whats-hows-and-whys.md): Overview of the Dotkernel Headless Platform architecture, its two main components (Dotkernel API and Dotkernel Admin), how to use them together or separately, and the benefits of the combined setup.
- [Dotkernel Queue - Asynchronous Execution in Dotkernel Headless Platform](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/dotkernel-queue-asynchronous-execution-in-dotkernel-headless-platform.md): Overview of Dotkernel Queue, a Symfony Messenger based component for running time-consuming or resource-intensive operations asynchronously via background workers in the Dotkernel Headless Platform.
- [DotMaker - Generate common code in Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/dotmaker-generate-common-code-in-dotkernel.md): Overview of dotkernel/dot-maker, the CLI tool that generates project files and directories matching the Dotkernel file structure, and how to use it to scaffold modules and individual code items.
- [Evolution Pattern versus API Versioning](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/evolution-pattern-versus-api-versioning.md): How Dotkernel weighs an evolution pattern against API versioning when changing an API, and the sunsetting mechanism used in Dotkernel API to announce breaking changes.
- [Implementing Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) in Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/implementing-time-based-one-time-password-totp-in-dotkernel.md): Tutorial on installing and using dot-totp to add two-factor authentication (2FA) with time-based one-time passwords to Dotkernel Admin, including required files, database changes, and the resulting user flow.
- [Shared Core Submodule in Dotkernel Headless Platform](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/shared-core-submodule-in-dotkernel-headless-platform.md): An explanation of the Core submodule pattern in Dotkernel's Headless Platform, and step-by-step instructions for extracting it into a shared Git submodule.
- [Version 7 adds PostgreSQL, Native UUID and PHP 8.5](http://localhost:8080/headless-platform/version-7-adds-postgresql-native-uuid-and-php-8-5.md): Overview of Dotkernel API and Admin's v7 release, which adds native UUID v7 support, PostgreSQL compatibility, PHP 8.5/8.4 support, and drops MySQL support.

## Dotkernel API

*REST API package - auth, content negotiation, OpenAPI*

- [API Client Migration: From Postman to Bruno](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/api-client-migration-from-postman-to-bruno.md): Why the Dotkernel team is considering switching their API testing client from Postman to the offline-focused, Git-native Bruno.
- [API Endpoint to Collect Client Errors](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/api-endpoint-to-collect-client-errors.md): How Dotkernel API's error-report endpoint lets frontend clients submit and log errors that occur on the user's machine.
- [Content Negotiation in Dotkernel REST API](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/content-negotiation-in-dotkernel-rest-api.md): How content negotiation works in RESTful APIs, who decides the data format, and how Dotkernel API implements it.
- [Dotkernel API 1.0.0 Released](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/dotkernel-api-1-0-0-released.md): Announcement of the Dotkernel API 1.0.0 release, a Zend Expressive 3 application for quickly building APIs, including the libraries it uses and the features it offers out of the box.
- [Dotkernel API Client Side Authorization](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/dotkernel-api-client-side-authorization.md): How a client application authorizes against a backend built with Dotkernel API, from the authorization request to using the access token.
- [Dotkernel API Server Side Authorization](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/dotkernel-api-server-side-authorization.md): How to configure server-side authorization in Dotkernel API, covering no-auth, authentication and authorization access levels, role inheritance, and route permissions.
- [Dotkernel API versus Laminas API Tools](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/dotkernel-api-versus-laminas-api-tools.md): A feature-by-feature comparison of Laminas API Tools and Dotkernel API, showing why Dotkernel API is a solid alternative now that Laminas API Tools is archived.
- [Error reporting endpoint in Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/error-reporting-endpoint-in-dotkernel-api.md): How the Dotkernel API error reporting endpoint lets frontend applications securely report bugs and data errors back to the API, including server-side and frontend setup.
- [How to implement MailChimp in Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/how-to-implement-mailchimp-in-dotkernel-api.md): A step-by-step guide to integrating MailChimp into a Dotkernel API instance using the drewm/mailchimp-api library, from installation to wiring up a factory in the ConfigProvider.
- [OpenAPI implementation in Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel-api/openapi-implementation-in-dotkernel-api.md): An overview of the OpenAPI Specification, why it complements tools like Postman, and how Dotkernel API implements OpenAPI documentation across its modules.

## Architecture Deep Dive

*request lifecycle and application bootstrapping*

- [ConfigProvider - Bootstrap Modern PHP Applications](http://localhost:8080/architecture/configprovider-bootstrap-modern-php-applications.md): An overview of the ConfigProvider pattern used in Laminas/Mezzio-based applications, including Dotkernel, to bootstrap middleware pipelines and dependency injection.
- [Request Lifecycle for a Mezzio-Based Application](http://localhost:8080/architecture/request-lifecycle-for-a-mezzio-based-application.md): A step-by-step walkthrough of how Dotkernel Light, a Mezzio-based application, handles an HTTP request from bootstrap through to the emitted response.
- [Understanding Middleware](http://localhost:8080/architecture/understanding-middleware.md): An introduction to middleware in PHP web applications: what it is, what it's used for, how PSR-15 defines it, and how it's called within an application's pipeline.

## How to's

*practical guides - migrations, CORS, PSR-7, routing*

- [CORS policy setup in Dotkernel using mezzio-cors](http://localhost:8080/how-to/cors-policy-setup-in-dotkernel-using-mezzio-cors.md): A walkthrough of fixing the classic 'No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header' CORS error in a Dotkernel application by installing and configuring the mezzio-cors package.
- [Creating admin accounts in Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/how-to/creating-admin-accounts-in-dotkernel-api.md): How to create admin accounts in Dotkernel API v3 and later, using either the protected POST /admin endpoint or the admin:create terminal command.
- [Database migrations and how to use them](http://localhost:8080/how-to/database-migrations-and-how-to-use-them.md): An overview of using database migrations and seeders in the Dotkernel stack via the 'php dot' command, covering setup, workflow best practices, and the difference between migrations and seeders.
- [Doctrine Cache in Mezzio and Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/how-to/doctrine-cache-in-mezzio-and-dotkernel.md): How to configure Doctrine's metadata, query, and result caches (via PhpFileCache) in a Mezzio/Dotkernel application, with usage examples on a query builder and a Doctrine Paginator-based collection.
- [Generating a doctrine migration without dropping custom tables](http://localhost:8080/how-to/generating-a-doctrine-migration-without-dropping-custom-tables.md): How to run doctrine-migrations diff without generating DROP TABLE statements for unmapped custom tables, using the --filter-expression option.
- [Implementation of SEO friendly URL in an generic Laminas Mezzio app](http://localhost:8080/how-to/implementation-of-seo-friendly-url-in-an-generic-laminas-mezzio-app.md): How to add human-readable, SEO-friendly URL slugs to a Mezzio/Doctrine application using the gedmo/doctrine-extensions package.
- [Installing AlmaLinux 10 in WSL2: PHP, MariaDB, Composer, PhpMyadmin](http://localhost:8080/how-to/installing-almalinux-10-in-wsl2-php-mariadb-composer-phpmyadmin.md): A recipe for setting up a full PHP development environment on AlmaLinux 10 under WSL2, covering installation, requirements, and running applications directly or via virtual hosts.
- [List available endpoints in Dotkernel API using dot-cli](http://localhost:8080/how-to/list-available-endpoints-in-dotkernel-api-using-dot-cli.md): How to use dot-cli's route:list command to display, and filter, all available endpoints in a Dotkernel API 3 application.
- [Migrating Dotkernel 3 from Zend Expressive 2 to Zend Expressive 3](http://localhost:8080/how-to/migrating-dotkernel-3-from-zend-expressive-2-to-zend-expressive-3.md): A walkthrough of migrating a Dotkernel 3 application with controller-based middleware from Zend Expressive 2 to Zend Expressive 3, covering dependency, configuration, and pipeline changes.
- [Replacing dot-console with dot-cli based on laminas-cli](http://localhost:8080/how-to/replacing-dot-console-with-dot-cli-based-on-laminas-cli.md): How to install and configure dot-cli, Dotkernel's laminas-cli based replacement for the abandoned dot-console package, including its built-in FileLocker locking system.
- [Using Postman for documentation in Dotkernel API 3](http://localhost:8080/how-to/using-postman-for-documentation-in-dotkernel-api-3.md): A walkthrough of using Postman to create, maintain, and export API documentation for Dotkernel API 3, including collections, environments, requests, and built-in security features.
- [Using the URLGenerator work in FastRoute](http://localhost:8080/how-to/using-the-urlgenerator-work-in-fastroute.md): A how-to on avoiding FastRoute's slash-suffix quirk when declaring routes in Dotkernel 3, and on referencing routes by name via the URLGenerator in controllers and Twig views.
- [What is cross origin token redemption?](http://localhost:8080/how-to/what-is-cross-origin-token-redemption.md): An explanation of cross-origin token redemption, the technique for securely verifying and redeeming a token issued on one domain when it's used on another, including how JWT and OAuth 2.0 implement it.
- [What is PSR-7 and how to use it](http://localhost:8080/how-to/what-is-psr-7-and-how-to-use-it.md): A practical reference to PSR-7's HTTP message interfaces and a cheatsheet-style walkthrough of working with headers and message bodies using Zend Diactoros.

Consider It Solved](http://localhost:8080/best-practice/zf-is-retired-laminas-mvc-is-retiring-consider-it-solved.md): What the Laminas MVC retirement announcement means, why legacy MVC platforms are a liability, and how Apidemia helps teams migrate to the Mezzio middleware architecture.

## Dotkernel 3

*the v3 rewrite on Zend Expressive/Mezzio*

- [Dotkernel Admin V4](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/dotkernel-admin-v4.md): An overview of Dotkernel Admin V4, released 19 July 2022 on Mezzio, covering its demo credentials and key features: PHP 8.1 support, configurability, authorization guards, CLI commands, routing, and its Bootstrap-based frontend.
- [Dotkernel Admin version 3 launched](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/dotkernel-admin-version-3-launched.md): Announcement of Dotkernel Admin version 3, a Bootstrap and Doctrine based admin panel built on Mezzio, including its GitHub source, live demo, and version 3 changelog requirements.
- [Dotkernel API: architecture and components](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/dotkernel-api-architecture-and-components.md): An overview of Dotkernel API's architecture and core components, covering Doctrine ORM, documentation, HAL, CORS, OAuth 2.0, email, configuration, routing, commands, the file locker, PSR standards, and testing.
- [Dotkernel Frontend version 3 launched](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/dotkernel-frontend-version-3-launched.md): Announcement of Dotkernel Frontend version 3, a Mezzio-based PHP application, including its GitHub source, live demo, and version 3 changelog requirements.
- [Dotkernel3 - Stable Release version 1.0](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/dotkernel3-stable-release-version-1-0.md): Dotkernel3's stable 1.0 release adds Zend Expressive 3 and PSR-15 middleware support, listing what's new, what changed for existing middleware, and every package updated or removed.
- [PHP 8.3 support in Dotkernel Admin](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/php-8-3-support-in-dotkernel-admin.md): A rundown of the backward incompatibilities and dependency updates involved in adding PHP 8.3 support to Dotkernel Admin, released in version 4.3.1.
- [PHP 8.3 support in Dotkernel API](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/php-8-3-support-in-dotkernel-api.md): Dotkernel API (now v4.2.1) was updated to support PHP 8.2 and PHP 8.3, dropping PHP 8.1, updating dependencies, and replacing the removed PhpFileCache with the new dot-cache package.
- [PHP 8.3 support in Dotkernel Frontend](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel3/php-8-3-support-in-dotkernel-frontend.md): The Dotkernel team updated the Frontend application to version 4.2.0 to support PHP 8.3, dropping PHP 8.1 and the PhpFileCache class along the way.

## Core Components

*the core framework - dot-* components (caching, logging, mail, dependency injection), Doctrine integration, and getting started with Dotkernel Light*

- [Autologin using Cookie / Remember Me in Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/autologin-using-cookie-remember-me-in-dotkernel.md): A step-by-step guide to implementing a Remember Me / autologin feature in Dotkernel Frontend.
- [Avoid routing through bootstrap of non existent files](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/avoid-routing-through-bootstrap-of-non-existent-files.md): How to stop missing static files from being routed through the bootstrap and logging out users whose session regenerates on each request.
- [Dependency Injection made easy in Laminas/Mezzio applications](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/dependency-injection-made-easy-in-laminas-mezzio-applications.md): Introduces Dotkernel's dot-dependency-injection package, which autowires constructor dependencies in Laminas/Mezzio applications via a PHP attribute instead of a hand-written factory per class.
- [Disambiguation: Dotkernel 1 and Dotkernel 3](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/disambiguation-dotkernel-1-and-dotkernel-3.md): Clarifies what Dotkernel 1 and Dotkernel 3 are, how they differ architecturally, and which version is meant when someone simply says 'Dotkernel'.
- [Doctrine cache using symfony/cache](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/doctrine-cache-using-symfony-cache.md): How to enable and configure the dotkernel/dot-cache component, a wrapper around symfony/cache, to cache Doctrine's result, metadata, query, and hydration data in Dotkernel Admin.
- [Doctrine enum implementation in Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/doctrine-enum-implementation-in-dotkernel.md): How Dotkernel adopted Doctrine ORM 3.2's EnumType support to replace loosely-enforced string-based status columns with PHP enums backed by a custom DBAL type.
- [Dotkernel Light - Starting with Mezzio microframework and Laminas components](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/dotkernel-light-starting-with-mezzio-microframework-and-laminas-components.md): Dotkernel Light is a stripped-down version of Dotkernel Frontend built on Mezzio and Laminas components, keeping only routing, templating, error handling, and tests, for a gentler learning curve.
- [Dotkernel Light: the best choice for your presentation site](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/dotkernel-light-the-best-choice-for-your-presentation-site.md): A walkthrough of using Dotkernel Light to build a simple presentation site: adding new pages, managing assets, and configuring Twitter/OpenGraph cards, the top menu, and the footer.
- [Handling and Logging errors with dot-errorhandler and dot-log](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/handling-and-logging-errors-with-dot-errorhandler-and-dot-log.md): A guide to using dotkernel/dot-errorhandler alongside dot-log (or zend-log) to log errors in Zend Expressive applications, covering its two handler types, configuration, and how it was tested.
- [How to build this website starting from Dotkernel Light](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/how-to-build-this-website-starting-from-dotkernel-light.md): How this blog itself came together: starting from the Dotkernel Light starter project, then following the Tutorial 101 to add Doctrine ORM and load real data into the database.
- [How to group log files by date using dot-log](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/how-to-group-log-files-by-date-using-dot-log.md): How dot-log Version 3.1.1 lets you use datetime formatter strings in the stream option of a log writer, so log files get grouped by date.
- [Logging with dot-log in Zend Expressive and Dotkernel](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/logging-with-dot-log-in-zend-expressive-and-dotkernel.md): How to wire up, configure and use the dot-log component (compatible with zend-log) within Dotkernel, Zend Expressive, or any project using Zend Service Manager.
- [Replacing laminas-mail with Symfony mailer in dot-mail](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/replacing-laminas-mail-with-symfony-mailer-in-dot-mail.md): Why and how Dotkernel replaced the abandoned laminas/laminas-mail package with symfony/mailer inside dotkernel/dot-mail, including configuration changes and the upgrade path to version 5.
- [Templating in Dotkernel3](http://localhost:8080/dotkernel/templating-in-dotkernel3.md): Dotkernel3 replaces its 10-year-old templating engine with Twig, gaining layouts, loops, variables, and escaping while keeping the familiarity of HTML.

*general PHP tooling, environments, IDEs, security*

- [Floating-Point Arithmetic - Why is (int)((0.7+0.1)*10) = 7 ?](http://localhost:8080/php-development/floating-point-arithmetic-why-is-int-0-7-0-1-10-7.md): An explanation of why PHP's floating-point arithmetic and int casting can produce unexpected results like (int)((0.7+0.1)*10) = 7 instead of 8.

- [Protection against SQL Injection using PDO and Zend Framework - part 2](http://localhost:8080/php-development/protection-against-sql-injection-using-pdo-and-zend-framework-part-2.md): A closer look at Zend_Db's query, fetchAll, insert, update, and delete methods, and where SQL injection can still slip through even with prepared statements.
- [Static Analysis - Replacing Psalm with PHPStan](http://localhost:8080/php-development/static-analysis-replacing-psalm-with-phpstan.md): Why Dotkernel replaced Psalm with PHPStan for static analysis, and a walkthrough of updating composer.json, CI, and configuration files to run PHPStan checks.

- [Mezzio app development in WSL2](http://localhost:8080/php-development/mezzio-app-development-in-wsl2.md) *(PHP Development)*: A step-by-step guide to installing a Mezzio application (Dotkernel API) inside WSL2, running it on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.
- [Intro to jQuery](http://localhost:8080/javascript/intro-to-jquery.md) *(Javascript)*: A short introduction to jQuery basics for early Dotkernel developers switching from Dojo, covering the jQuery object, selectors, DOM manipulation, events, and Ajax.
- [FIX: Installing PEAR packages with PHP 7.2](http://localhost:8080/php-troubleshooting/fix-installing-pear-packages-with-php-7-2.md) *(PHP Troubleshooting)*: How to fix the 'Cannot use result of built-in function in write context' PEAR error on PHP 7.2 by patching Archive_Tar's func_get_args() call, and how to reinstall the affected packages afterward.
- [Where is the intl PHP extension? Problem solved!](http://localhost:8080/php-troubleshooting/where-is-the-intl-php-extension-problem-solved.md) *(PHP Troubleshooting)*: Common causes of 'missing intl PHP extension' errors and step-by-step fixes for installing or enabling the Intl extension on Linux and Windows PHP setups.
- [MIT versus LGPL in practice: Dotkernel case](http://localhost:8080/licensing/mit-versus-lgpl-in-practice-dotkernel-case.md) *(Licensing)*: How Dotkernel handled discovering an LGPL v3 dependency in one of its MIT-licensed packages.
- [Code Quality: How to setup phpcs in PHPStorm](http://localhost:8080/phpstorm/code-quality-how-to-setup-phpcs-in-phpstorm.md) *(PHPStorm)*: A step-by-step guide to configuring PHP_CodeSniffer (phpcs) in PHPStorm, both when cloning a new project and when fixing an existing project that isn't yet reporting code quality issues.
- [Sunsetting PEAR Channel for Zend Framework 1](http://localhost:8080/zend-framework/sunsetting-pear-channel-for-zend-framework-1.md) *(Zend Framework)*: Dotkernel announces the sunsetting of its unofficial PEAR channel for Zend Framework 1, citing PHP 8 compatibility issues and aging server infrastructure.
- [Zend Framework 1 End-of-Life](http://localhost:8080/zend-framework/zend-framework-1-end-of-life.md) *(Zend Framework)*: Announcement that Zend Framework 1 has reached End-of-Life (EOL) status following the release of Zend Framework 3, with security updates continuing only until 28 September 2016.
